Thursday 12 November 2026 · 25 stories
Morning Brief
Nifty 50 rose 0.84% to 25,255 on narrow participation
Today’s read
The biggest names carried the session. The fifty most traded stocks returned +2.55% weighted by turnover, against +0.96% for the median stock, a gap of 1.6 percentage points, so most stocks did worse than the busiest names suggest.

Ashoka Buildcon Limited rose 11.1% on 106 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about an order win, “Receipt of Letter of Acceptance (LOA) for Solar PV Power Plant in Bhutan”.

Makers Laboratories Limited rose 16.5% on 96 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Exide, Amara Raja rush to monetize $1 billion Li-ion cell lines as investor questions mount”.

TRANSWORLD SHIPPING LINES LIMITED fell 1.4% on 88 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Exide, Amara Raja rush to monetize $1 billion Li-ion cell lines as investor questions mount”.

Gujarat Natural Resources Limited rose 5.1% on 167 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “BHEL shares up 3.5% on Power Grid order for Gujarat synchronous condensers”.

Dollar near one-month high as yen edges toward 160
The US dollar index traded near a one-month high as the yen weakened toward 160 per dollar due to widening interest rate differentials. A firmer dollar weakens the rupee, increasing landed crude costs for Indian oil refiners and prompting foreign fund outflows from domestic equities. Indian IT exporters gain from currency depreciation, while net importing sectors face margin pressure.

Ashoka Buildcon shares jump 15% on ₹866 crore NHAI expressway contract
Ashoka Buildcon secured an ₹866.6 crore contract from the National Highways Authority of India for eight-lane Vadodara-Mumbai Expressway works. The win expands its engineering, procurement, and construction order book, improving revenue visibility over a two-year execution timeline. Sustained EBITDA margins will depend on steel and cement price stability during execution.
InfrastructureBS Markets
Exide, Amara Raja rush to monetize $1 billion Li-ion cell lines as investor questions mount
Exide Industries and Amara Raja Energy are redirecting their combined $1 billion lithium-ion cell capacity toward telecom and energy storage projects as domestic electric vehicle adoption slows. Selling to industrial buyers provides immediate cash flow to offset heavy capital expenditure and asset-turnover lag. Lower realization margins in industrial storage may depress overall return on capital employed compared to original automotive projections.
Mint Companies
BHEL shares up 3.5% on Power Grid order for Gujarat synchronous condensers
Bharat Heavy Electricals received a contract from Power Grid Corporation to supply two grid-stabilizing synchronous condensers in Gujarat. The order diversifies BHEL's order book beyond traditional thermal equipment into specialized power transmission infrastructure. Execution on schedule will confirm margin expansion in its industrial equipment division over the next two financial years.

Your themes
Nvidia shares recover 4.5% after steep sell-off; China spy probe and November 17 earnings to test investor confidence
Nvidia rose 4.5% after AI infrastructure client CoreWeave posted strong revenues, partially offsetting recent losses driven by China trade probes. The rebound matters for Indian IT services exporters because sustained hyperscaler capital expenditure directly supports global enterprise IT budgets and digital transformation spending. The key metric to watch is Nvidia's data center revenue guidance on November 17.

Nvidia may oust Jensen Huang after second affair with employee, board working with outside firm to identify successor
Nvidia's board is evaluating executive succession following workplace misconduct allegations against chief executive Jensen Huang. Leadership instability at the world's primary semiconductor vendor could trigger broader US tech market volatility, prompting foreign institutional investors to temporarily reallocate capital toward emerging markets like India. The outcome of the board's internal governance review will determine immediate market impact.

Baird downgrades Nvidia on China curbs, AI demand worries
Baird downgraded Nvidia citing US export restrictions to China and signs of softening hardware demand. Reduced global semiconductor momentum directly pressures Indian engineering R&D and tech services providers that rely on global chipmaker clients for product engineering revenues. A decline in Nvidia's forward order book in upcoming quarterly disclosures would confirm this demand slowdown.

India emerges as standout emerging market after US midterm elections: Shriram Research
Brent crude declines combined with foreign capital rotating out of mega-cap US technology stocks are improving relative risk-reward for Indian equities. Lower oil prices reduce input costs for domestic margin-sensitive sectors like paints, auto, and chemicals, while supporting the rupee. Net foreign portfolio investor flow data over the next fortnight will confirm whether capital is actively shifting into Indian large-caps.

Nifty eyes record as largecaps lead charge on strong corporate earnings
Large-cap quarterly earnings beats and softer crude oil prices have brought domestic benchmark indices near record levels. Margin expansion across banking and consumer majors is sustaining elevated market valuation multiples by supporting aggregate earnings growth expectations. Second-quarter aggregate earnings growth exceeding 15% year-on-year across Nifty 50 constituents would validate this upward momentum.

Benchmarks rise nearly 1%; auto, bank stocks lead gains amid FPI inflows
Foreign portfolio investors turned net buyers as benchmark indices rose nearly 1%, led by rate-sensitive banking and auto stocks. Reversing recent net selling, foreign capital flows directly support large-cap valuations and ease near-term liquidity tightness across financial sector balance sheets. NSDL daily flow data over the next three sessions will confirm whether this marks a structural reallocation or routine short covering.
BS Markets · +1 other
Sterling drops against firmer dollar as markets price in a hawkish Fed
Sterling fell against a strengthening US dollar as traders priced in a higher-for-longer policy rate path from the Federal Reserve. A firmer dollar index typically pressures emerging market currencies, raising domestic imported input costs while offering valuation tailwinds for Indian net exporters like IT and pharmaceuticals. The upcoming US CPI print will clarify if dollar strength persists to curb foreign portfolio flows into India.

Fairfax likely to exit India's IIFL Finance, sources say
Fairfax Financial Holdings plans to fully exit its stake in IIFL Finance through secondary market block transactions. The divestment creates a short-term equity supply overhang, potentially compressing valuation multiples for the non-banking financial company. Institutional focus will shift back to retail loan book growth and asset quality once the block trade pricing establishes a clear secondary market floor.

Macro and economy
India's net direct tax collections rise 11.8% from April 1 to Nov 10
Net direct tax collections grew 11.8% year-on-year to reach ₹12.11 lakh crore between April 1 and November 10. Healthy tax receipts reduce fiscal deficit risks, keeping government borrowing in check and anchoring sovereign bond yields. Lower yields protect capital expenditure outlays for listed infrastructure, capital goods, and cement companies, with mid-December advance tax receipts offering the next earnings validation.

Bajaj Finance launches ₹11,700 crore QIP at 5% discount to closing price
Bajaj Finance launched an ₹11,700 crore qualified institutional placement at an indicative price offering a 5% discount to the closing price. The equity dilution will temporarily lower return on equity, but the fresh capital strengthens Tier-1 capital adequacy and lowers overall borrowing costs. This enhanced balance sheet headroom supports assets under management growth across consumer and commercial lending segments.

Japan wholesale inflation accelerates, keeps alive rate hike view
Accelerating Japanese wholesale inflation has no direct transmission mechanism to Indian corporate earnings or domestic equity market valuations.

Tata Power approves ₹11,871 crore pumped storage project in Maharashtra
Tata Power's board approved an ₹11,871 crore capital expenditure for a 1.8 GW pumped storage hydro project in Maharashtra, scheduled for completion in 51 months. This project expands the company's contracted asset base and long-term earnings visibility in grid-scale energy storage. The large outlay expands capital goods order books for equipment suppliers like BHEL, though execution delays remain a key monitorable.

Promoter encumbrances increase refinancing risk and can cap valuation multiples across TVS group companies if equity volatility triggers margin calls. ArcelorMittal's $900 million Brazil expansion plan trudges along as imports weigh on economics
ArcelorMittal slowed its $900 million Brazilian expansion as cheap Chinese steel imports eroded project economics. Chinese overcapacity continues to flood global markets, driving down international steel prices and weakening export realizations for Indian steelmakers such as Tata Steel and JSW Steel. Monthly domestic import volumes and landed price spreads will confirm if Indian steel operating margins face further compression.

CoreWeave results lift tech stocks as dollar gains - RTHK News
CoreWeave reported strong financial results that boosted US technology shares, while the US dollar index strengthened simultaneously. Robust AI infrastructure demand signals sustained enterprise technology spending, providing revenue visibility for Indian IT services exporters like Infosys and TCS. However, a stronger dollar encourages foreign portfolio investors to reallocate capital away from emerging market equities back to the US.

Wall Street Says the Fed Made a Mistake. Now More Rate Hikes May Be Coming - The Wealth Advisor
US money markets began pricing in higher interest rates after economic data prompted concerns that the Federal Reserve paused rate hikes prematurely. Elevated US Treasury yields narrow the interest rate differential between India and the United States, accelerating foreign portfolio debt and equity outflows. This capital flight pressures the rupee and compresses valuation multiples for high-duration Indian growth equities.

Geopolitics
Dollar rises toward two-week high on Fed rate hike bets - سانا
The US dollar index climbed toward a two-week high as investors repriced Federal Reserve interest rate expectations upward. A strengthening dollar depreciates the Indian rupee, driving up input costs for imported raw materials and crude oil. This currency pressure threatens gross margins for domestic consumer staples and industrial manufacturers, while benefiting net-exporter sectors like pharmaceuticals and software.
Fed and rates
COMMENTARY: A 50 bps rate hike? Warsh's Fed has a comms problem - Reuters
Market commentary highlights rising communication risks around Kevin Warsh's prospective Fed leadership, raising fears of an aggressive 50 basis point US rate hike. Higher US interest rates widen yield differentials, triggering foreign portfolio outflows from Indian equities, weakening the rupee, and weighing on high-valuation IT and financial stocks. Upcoming US payrolls data will confirm whether labor market strength supports such hawkish policy shifts.
Fed and rates
German economic adviser sees higher US tariff risks after midterms
A German economic panel warned that US protectionist tariff risks will escalate after midterm elections, threatening European industrial output. Weakening European growth and trade fragmentation reduce export demand for Indian engineering goods, chemicals, and auto components, though softer global oil prices could offset margin pressure. Upcoming Eurozone manufacturing PMI readings will reveal whether European industrial orders are already contracting ahead of potential trade barriers.
